thread:
emily: FYI customer hit a double-charge scenario after a streaming truncation + reconnect that triggered a tool call retry. Logs attached below, short thread so we can decide a mitigation.

emily: ```
[stream] session_id=abc123 route=us-west-1 model=redwood-13b-v2 state=truncated reason=content_filter tokens_emitted=18 billing_state=provisional
[toolcall] id=tcall-77 invoked=true status=timeout billing_charged=false
[resume] new_session=def456 route=us-east-2 model=redwood-13b-v2 tokens_emitted=42 billing_state=confirmed
```

rahul: Ugh. Looks like affinity was lost (route changed) and the resumed path created a confirmed ledger entry while the provisional from the truncated stream was never reconciled. That explains the double bill.

sam: Two separate problems: (1) when truncation triggers a toolcall we sometimes mark provisional tokens, (2) resume on a different route creates a new confirmed entry instead of mapping to the provisional one.

jordan: Do we have a session->ledger binding today? I thought provisional credits were keyed to a session id but if the client reconnects with a different session we lose linkage.

rahul: Current flow: provisional credits tied to ephemeral stream_id, not durable across resume. Resume uses a new session_id if routing fallback happens. We intentionally made session IDs cheap for scaling, but that breaks billing idempotency in these failure cases.

liz: UX question: how will this surface in the console? Customers reported seeing two charges but no clue which was provisional. We should show provisional vs confirmed in the request timeline.

sam: Proposal A (short-term): attach a durable session_trace_id to every request (client-supplied or generated at first connect) that we carry across route failovers. Use that key in the ledger to merge provisional/confirmed entries. Also emit telemetry tag billing_state:(provisional|confirmed) and resume_count.

sam: Example telemetry event we can add: ```
billing_event: session_trace_id=abc123 tokens=18 source=stream reason=truncation state=provisional route=us-west-1
billing_event: session_trace_id=abc123 tokens=42 source=stream reason=resume state=confirmed route=us-east-2
```

rahul: Proposal B (longer-term): change semantics so toolcalls are billed on completion (confirmed) instead of at invocation time, but keep provisional credits for streaming bytes. That avoids charging for retries where the toolcall never completed and the tool was never actually used. Downsides: increases complexity around async toolcalls and external billing.

jordan: For quotas: if we hold provisional credits against a quota, quota accounting needs to reflect provisional reservations (reduce available quota) but allow automatic release on rollback within X seconds. Otherwise customers see weird quota cliffs.

liz: Console UX: show a yellow "provisional" badge inline on the request row with hover text "May be reconciled; final billing will be shown after processing". Add a filter "show provisional charges" for billing view.

rahul: Near-term mitigation I can implement this sprint: (1) session_trace_id passthrough + ledger keying, (2) telemetry tags (billing_state,resume_count,session_trace_id), (3) console flag that surfaces provisional rows. Will need a short migration to reconcile existing orphan provisional entries.

billing-bot: Automated note: created ticket BILL-1123 "session_trace_id billing reconciliation" and assigned to @rahul.

emily: Thanks. Action items: rahul -> implement session_trace_id + telemetry (this sprint), sam -> add ledger merge logic + rollback window proposal, jordan -> spec console badge and provisional filter, liz -> coordinate docs/announce. We'll follow up with a small postmortem once we reconcile the customer's charges.

sam: One caveat: if we keep provisional tokens reserved against quota we must cap reservation time (30s?) to avoid long-held reservations. Recommend 60s default with config per-customer.

rahul: Agreed. I'll add a config flag route_affinity_ttl=30s and provisional_reservation_ttl=60s. If a resume occurs within TTL we reconcile; else we let provisional expire and leave final confirmed charge as-is.

jordan: Can we add a log line on reconcile that maps provisional_id -> confirmed_id so support can stitch customer complaints? That would make audits easier.

rahul: Yep. We'll emit reconcile events with mapping. Example: `reconcile_event: provisional=evt-900 confirmed=evt-901 session_trace_id=abc123`.

liz: Sounds good. I'll draft console mockups and a short customer-facing note.

emily: Cool — thanks all, keep the thread updated if anything blocks the implementation.
